key_insight: A unified analytical model can diagnose losses and guide rational design for both BIJ and SEJ photoelectrochemical cells using the same physically meaningful parameters.
engineering_relevance: The framework turns experimental current-voltage curves into actionable bottleneck maps, helping engineers choose materials and interventions such as co-catalysts, nanostructures, and junction optimization.
method: Fits PEC current-voltage data to decompose losses into thermodynamic, optical, recombination, and interfacial terms
Generates ideal/real efficiency maps to identify theoretical limits and material-selection windows
Uses Sankey diagrams to visualize solar-energy flow from absorption to chemical output
evidence_signal: The model was validated against literature data across solar water splitting, CO2 reduction, NH3 synthesis, and solar redox flow batteries.
watch_item: Accuracy depends on the quality of experimental IV fitting and the assumption that the chosen loss categories capture the dominant mechanisms in a given device.
paper_title: From Loss Diagnosis to Rational Design: A Unified Analytical Model for Photoelectrochemical Cells
